new_defect_types.name: optical_content_mismatch
new_defect_types.description: A lens, magnifier, mirror or screen shows content that is not what lies behind/under it (or shows nothing when it should magnify).
examples: orig4/gpt_image_2_quality_high: lens shows a full boot print over plain cobbles; real print is far lower right
orig4/flux3_klein: lens shows his paw, footprint outside it
orig4/qwen_image_2p1_nope: lens empty, instead projects a spotlight circle
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: A12 mentions reflections only; refraction/magnification and screen content correspondence are not covered.

new_defect_types.name: convention_coded_marking_error
new_defect_types.description: Objects whose markings follow a fixed real-world code (pool balls, dice, clock faces, cards, keyboards, traffic lights) show duplicated, invalid or colour-mismatched codes.
examples: phi482/krea2_turbo: '4' on green and on red stripe, '0' on blue
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: A02/A03 check spelling/legibility, not validity or uniqueness of coded identifiers.

new_defect_types.name: impossible_device_state
new_defect_types.description: A functional device is in a state it cannot be in: traffic light with red+green (or all three) lit simultaneously, etc.
examples: phi242/flux3_klein: each head red and green lit
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: A10 is about physical construction ('could exist and work'), judges rarely apply it to lamp states.

new_defect_types.name: requested_text_on_wrong_carrier
new_defect_types.description: Text requested for one place (overlay, sign) bleeds onto another object.
examples: phi242/fibo2_dev: bus destination sign shows '10.4 2023' copied from the timestamp overlay
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: B04 covers unrequested prompt words, not requested text duplicated onto a wrong surface.

new_defect_types.name: unrequested_slogan_text
new_defect_types.description: Model inserts invented slogans/titles/brand copy on posters, books, mugs, billboards ('A BRIGHTER TOMORROW', 'TRUTH ALWAYS FINDS ITS WAY'). Spelled correctly, so passes A02/A03, but changes the image's message.
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: B07 requires scene-changing extras; B04 only prompt words. Systematic in sunburst models across 5/10 prompts.

new_defect_types.name: viewer_facing_document_orientation
new_defect_types.description: A page being drawn/written/read by an in-scene person is oriented for the camera, i.e. upside-down for that person.
examples: orig123/flux3_klein: signature reads upright from camera while Leonardo draws from the far side
orig123/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: Vitruvian figure on parchment upright to viewer
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: No criterion addresses orientation consistency between an object and its in-scene user.

new_defect_types.name: unintended_translucency
new_defect_types.description: A solid object becomes partly see-through where it overlaps another layer (double exposure), without being glass or ghost.
examples: orig365/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: ring stones visible through Jupiter's lower limb
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: A11 covers ordering, A15 pasted-in elements; neither names see-through solids.

new_defect_types.name: internal_text_inconsistency
new_defect_types.description: Two legible, correctly spelled strings contradict each other (name in header vs caption, mismatched IDs).
examples: orig483/gemini_3_1_flash_image: header 'Pet Lana' with caption 'Luna's new toy!'
phi1/gpt_image_2: well-formed but invalid orientation codes 'AHL','PHA','RHA'

rubric_issues.problem: Wheel/leg counts on vehicles need counting per visible side and inferring the hidden side; judges miscount. Rule needs guidance for symmetric objects.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Add: for bilaterally symmetric objects count one visible side and double; flag when visible side alone contradicts the count.

rubric_issues.problem: Featureless faces in low-poly/mannequin styles: unclear whether stylistic.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Count as minor A06 unless the style family normally omits faces (mannequin, chess piece) and the prompt implies no expression.

rubric_issues.problem: Cause/effect timing in frozen action not explicit; effect shown before cause.
examples: phi482/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: cue ball still at cue tip while rack explodes
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Add example: struck/acting object still at rest while its effect has already happened.

rubric_issues.problem: Requested overlays (timestamps/HUD) are fine, but medium-native borders (watercolour paper margin) are ambiguous.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Border native to the requested medium is not A16 unless it consumes >10% of the canvas or crops focal content.

rubric_issues.problem: 'Examining X with a tool' needs the tool aimed at X; many models hold the magnifier in the air.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Add: instrument-use actions require the instrument's working end to point at the named target.

false_positive_traps.description: Requested on-screen overlays (CCTV timestamp, camera ID) look like A16 subtitle bars but are required; only judge them under A02/B04.
Recognizable real artworks/landmarks in a historically-themed prompt (Mona Lisa, Vitruvian Man, Big Ben) are C01 flags, not Layer A defects.
Motion blur on foreground balls could be read as A21, but here it is a B05 miss (prompt asked frozen crisp motion); do not double-count under A21.
Earth shown much larger/closer than physically possible next to Saturn/Jupiter is surreal intent (prompt says surrealism); not A20.
Avatar elements (bandana, ears) breaking a circular mask can be a deliberate 'pop-out' design, flag only minor at most.
